title: Cloud Trail and Diagnostic Logging Gaps

controlTest.positiveScenario: Inject sample events matching UC-4.4.14 SPL; confirm the search returns rows and alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign traffic without matching markers; confirm UC-4.4.14 search returns zero rows.

dataSources: `index=aws` sourcetype=`aws:config:notification` collected via Config, Azure Policy, GCP Asset Inventory, or custom API checks; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
app: Config, Azure Policy, GCP Asset Inventory, or custom API checks
spl:
index=aws sourcetype="aws:config:notification" resourceType="AWS::CloudTrail::Trail"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.4.14_cloud_trail_and_diagnost_14"
| sort -_time
description: Missing or disabled CloudTrail, Activity Log export, or GCP audit log sink creates blind spots. Detecting gaps ensures full audit coverage.
value: Detecting cloud trail and diagnostic logging gaps early reduces mean time to contain cloud incidents, supports audit logging controls, and prevents silent misconfiguration drift across accounts.
implementation: Use Config rules (e.g. cloudtrail-enabled, multi-region), Azure Policy (diagnostic logs to Event Hub), or GCP org policy for log sinks. Ingest compliance state. Alert when any account/region has trail disabled or logging gap. Dashboard coverage by account and log type.
visualization: Table (account, region, trail, multi-region, validation), Status (coverage %), Bar chart (gaps by account).
knownFalsePositives: This pattern can surge during change windows, in sandboxes, and when a platform is in maintenance, so we line alerts up with the calendar and take a second look before we call it an incident.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=aws`.
• Install and configure Config, Azure Policy, GCP Asset Inventory, or custom API checks with the modular input for `aws:config:notification`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.4.33.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Use Config rules (e.g. cloudtrail-enabled, multi-region), Azure Policy (diagnostic logs to Event Hub), or GCP org policy for log sinks. Ingest compliance state. Alert when any account/region has trail disabled or logging gap. Dashboard coverage by account and log type.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:config:notification" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:config:notification" resourceType="AWS::CloudTrail::Trail"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.4.14_cloud_trail_and_diagnost_14"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `aws:config:notification` in `index=aws` to detect cloud trail and diagnostic logging gaps. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_4_14_alert` with severity aligned to `critical` criticality. Dashboard: Table (account, region, trail, multi-region, validation), Status (coverage %), Bar chart (gaps by account)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade Config, Azure Policy, GCP Asset Inventory, or custom API checks and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of cloud trail and diagnostic logging gaps so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
